claims.text: Oxidation resistance in high-temperature MPEAs is governed by the formation of stable, adherent oxide layers enriched in Al and Cr.
Al- and Cr-enriched oxide layers inhibit further oxidation.
Al- and Cr-enriched oxide layers help maintain structural stability.
Changing Al and Cr concentrations while holding other elements constant will alter oxide-layer formation and adherence.
Al preferentially oxidizes to form Al2O3.
Cr preferentially oxidizes to form Cr2O3.
Al2O3 and Cr2O3 are stable under the proposed high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Al2O3- and Cr2O3-rich scales act as diffusion barriers that reduce oxygen ingress.
Reduced oxygen ingress protects the alloy substrate from further degradation.
MPEAs with higher Al and Cr concentrations will have lower oxidation mass gain than MPEAs with lower Al and Cr concentrations under otherwise identical conditions.
MPEAs with higher Al and Cr concentrations will retain mechanical integrity better than MPEAs with lower Al and Cr concentrations.
The proposed governing behavior should hold in oxidizing environments at temperatures up to approximately 1200°C when the composition supports stable oxide-layer formation.
The Al and Cr concentration thresholds needed for optimal oxidation resistance may depend on interactions with other alloying elements.
